name: Anekathangavadeswarar Temple, Kanchipuram
deity: Shiva as Anekathangavadeswarar (Anekathangapadeswarar), the lingam said to have been installed by Vinayaka, with Kamakshi of Kanchipuram as the common consort
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu, sung in the Tevaram by Sundarar (8th century)
summary: On the lane to the Kailasanathar temple in Kanchipuram, a tiny shrine keeps the lingam that tradition says Vinayaka himself installed and worshipped — Kachi Anekathangapadam, sung by Sundarar.

sections.history: Kachi Anekathangapadam is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu. The Tevaram knows two shrines of this name: the northern one, sung by Sambandar, is identified with Gaurikund on the road to Kedarnath, and this one is set apart by the prefix Kachi, the old name of Kanchipuram. Sundarar sang its Lord in a pathigam gathered in the seventh book of the Tirumurai, and the name Anekatangapadam appears both in the hymns and in old inscriptions. The temple stands in the Pillaiyarpalayam area on the way from the town to the great Pallava temple of Kailasanathar, and is administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of Tamil Nadu.
sections.architecture: This is one of the smallest of Kanchipuram's Tevaram shrines: a compact enclosure with a single sanctum of Shiva and its attendant shrines, set on a very small campus close to the Kailasanathar temple. As at the city's other old Shiva temples, there is no separate shrine of the goddess. Its interest lies less in scale than in its place in the hymns and its bond with Vinayaka, whose presence is honoured here alongside the Lord he is said to have worshipped.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Vinayaka, the elephant-faced son of Shiva, installed this lingam and worshipped it to gain his father's blessing. In one telling the asura Kesi had seized Vallabhai, a maiden raised by the sage Marichi; armed with Shiva's grace, Vinayaka overcame Kesi and took Vallabhai as his consort. The Kanchi Puranam holds that worship at the shrine Vinayaka honoured frees the devotee from the round of rebirth.
sections.festivals: Pradosham and Maha Shivaratri are kept with special worship, together with Karthigai Deepam and the festivals of Vinayaka, whose story is bound to this shrine. Hours at this small temple can be short, so confirm timings and festival dates locally.
sections.experience: The shrine is easily missed — a quiet stop on the road to the Kailasanathar temple, best visited before or after that great Pallava monument. Pilgrims come to complete the round of Kanchipuram's Tevaram temples and to honour the Lord whom Vinayaka himself is remembered to have worshipped. Thirumetrali, Onakanthanthali and Ekambareswarar are all within a short auto ride.

visit.timings: This small temple may keep short opening hours, typically in the morning and again in the evening. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer areas, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in Pillaiyarpalayam, Kanchipuram, on the road from the town to the Kailasanathar temple by way of Putheri Street, a short auto ride from the Kanchipuram bus stand and railway station. Kanchipuram is linked by road to Chennai, Chengalpattu, Vellore and Arakkonam; Chennai International Airport, roughly 70 km away, is the nearest airport.
